cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Show Me the Score
cards.instruction: Find out how they measure success, what they stand to gain, and where you currently rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a tick beside every sandwich, like you. How far ahead does that put my stall?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those ticks mean gluten-free, not sold. We rank stalls by money raised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, qualifying sandwiches. What do you get for raising the most?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First choice of stall next year. I've raised eighty pounds; you've raised sixty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twenty-one more pounds puts me ahead of you. Does that get first choice, or is someone above us?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies allergy marks as scores; B2 exposes the mistake and A3 covers while investigating success metric, reward and A's actual rank.

responseLogic.evidence: B4 eighty versus sixty produces A5 twenty-one-pound target and question about overall first place.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains the system and B4 openly shares both reward and comparison, letting A learn without another argument.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 numbers to distinguish beating B from winning overall.

specificity.evidence: A1 sandwich stall and B2 gluten-free marks define the setting; A5 uses only established figures.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 exact twenty-one-pound comparison is purposeful and replaces the manufactured fee.
